cues.en: We now begin this section of the course on visualizing data.
cues.zh: 現在開始課程中，資料視覺化這一節。

cues.en: This is super important.
cues.zh: 這非常重要。

cues.en: It's really, really important to visualize data as much as possible.
cues.zh: 盡可能把資料視覺化，真的非常非常重要。

cues.en: I will stress this idea throughout the course.
cues.zh: 整門課，我會不斷強調這個想法。

cues.en: And in this section, I'm going to introduce you to the main ways of visualizing data.
cues.zh: 這一節，會介紹主要的資料視覺化方法。

cues.en: And so we begin with the bar plot.
cues.zh: 從長條圖開始。

cues.en: Let me start by giving you an example of a bar plot.
cues.zh: 先舉個長條圖的例子。

cues.en: Let's say we do an experiment, we do a survey, and we go around and we get a bunch of random people and we ask them, how do you get your news?
cues.zh: 假設做實驗、做問卷，找一批隨機的人，問他們：你如何取得新聞？

cues.en: Where do you get your news from?
cues.zh: 新聞來自哪裡？

cues.en: So we gave them choices, TV, newspaper, Internet or word of mouth.
cues.zh: 給他們選項：電視、報紙、網路，或口耳相傳。

cues.en: And we computed the percent of participants that responded yes to each one of these things.
cues.zh: 然後計算各個選項中，回答是的參與者百分比。

cues.en: So we might get data that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 得到的資料，可能長這樣。

cues.en: So around 40 percent of people said, yes, they watch TV or they get their news from the TV.
cues.zh: 大約 40% 的人說，是的，他們看電視，或從電視取得新聞。

cues.en: And, you know, like 80 or 90 percent of people say they get their news from the Internet and so on.
cues.zh: 大概 80% 或 90% 的人說從網路取得新聞，依此類推。

cues.en: So this is a bar plot.
cues.zh: 這就是長條圖。

cues.en: You can see why it's called a bar plot.
cues.zh: 可以看出為什麼叫長條圖。

cues.en: It is a plot made out of borrus.
cues.zh: 因為圖是由長條組成。

cues.en: Pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 非常直接。

cues.en: So here's a question for you.
cues.zh: 問你一個問題。

cues.en: What kind of data are these?
cues.zh: 這是哪種資料？

cues.en: What is the data type that I am illustrating here?
cues.zh: 這裡展示的資料類型是什麼？

cues.en: Have you figured it out?
cues.zh: 想出來了嗎？

cues.en: Well, of course, it's nominal.
cues.zh: 當然是名目資料。

cues.en: These are nominal data because they are categorical.
cues.zh: 這是名目資料，因為它們是類別。

cues.en: They are categories.
cues.zh: 它們是類別。

cues.en: And there is no way to order them.
cues.zh: 而且無法排序。

cues.en: So you can't say word of mouth is higher than Internet, which is higher than newspaper and so on.
cues.zh: 不能說口耳相傳比網路高，網路又比報紙高，依此類推。

cues.en: So there is no intrinsic ordering between these different media.
cues.zh: 這些不同媒體之間，沒有內在順序。

cues.en: So these are nominal data.
cues.zh: 所以是名目資料。

cues.en: And now I would like to ask you a question more generally.
cues.zh: 現在想問一個更一般的問題。

cues.en: Which data types do you think can be shown in a bar plot?
cues.zh: 你認為哪些資料類型，可以用長條圖呈現？

cues.en: So this gives an example of nominal.
cues.zh: 這是名目資料的例子。

cues.en: And the question is, what other kinds of data are appropriate for a bar plot, if you like?
cues.zh: 問題是，其他哪些資料，也適合用長條圖？

cues.en: So I'm going to be asking questions to you very often throughout this course, if you like.
cues.zh: 整門課我會經常問你問題。

cues.en: I certainly encourage you to pause the video and take a moment to think of your answer if you want or if you need to.
cues.zh: 我當然鼓勵暫停影片，花點時間思考答案。如果想要，或需要，

cues.en: You can consult your notes back to several videos ago as the beginning of the what our data section about types of data.
cues.zh: 可以翻看前幾部影片的筆記，也就是「什麼是資料」那一節開頭，介紹資料類型的部分。

cues.en: Anyway, so the answer here is both kinds of categorical data.
cues.zh: 答案是，兩種類別資料都可以。

cues.en: So nominal and ordinal data can be shown in a bar plot, numerical data.
cues.zh: 名目與次序資料，都能用長條圖。至於數值資料，

cues.en: It can kind of be shown in a bar plot, but only for discrete numerical data.
cues.zh: 某種程度也能用長條圖，但僅限離散數值資料。

cues.en: And let me illustrates you why this is the case.
cues.zh: 來說明原因。

cues.en: So let's imagine we take a trip to Antarctica and we go around and we start talking to a bunch of king penguins.
cues.zh: 想像去南極旅行，四處找一些國王企鵝聊天。

cues.en: These are really large penguins.
cues.zh: 這些企鵝很大隻。

cues.en: Well, relatively large penguins.
cues.zh: 嗯，相對大隻。

cues.en: And we survey them and we want to know how tall are these different penguins?
cues.zh: 調查它們，想知道這些不同企鵝有多高。

cues.en: So we asked them how tall they are.
cues.zh: 所以問它們身高。

cues.en: And, you know, they get out a ruler and they tell us.
cues.zh: 它們拿出尺，告訴我們。

cues.en: Now, the thing is, height in centimeters is.
cues.zh: 問題是，以公分表示的身高，是，

cues.en: Ratio scale data.
cues.zh: 比率尺度資料。

cues.en: And one of the things that means is that there is an arbitrary precision.
cues.zh: 這代表其中一項性質，是精度可以任意細分。

cues.en: So the more precise your ruler, the more precise your your measurement is going to be.
cues.zh: 尺越精準，測量就越精細。

cues.en: And that means that no two penguins can possibly have exactly, exactly the same height with a really precise ruler.
cues.zh: 這代表如果尺非常精準，不可能有兩隻企鵝，身高完全完全相同。

cues.en: So instead, what we can do in order to create a bar plot is group the data group heights or disc critize the heights.
cues.zh: 所以為了建立長條圖，可以把資料、身高分組，也就是把身高離散化。

cues.en: So we're taking our data, which is actually continuous.
cues.zh: 原本的資料其實是連續的。

cues.en: It's it's random data.
cues.zh: 它是隨機資料。

cues.en: It is arbitrarily precise and it's not countable.
cues.zh: 精度可任意細分，而且不可數。

cues.en: And we group them into these bins.
cues.zh: 我們把它們分進這些區間。

cues.en: So this would be a bin for 60 to 70 centimetres and so on, up to 100 to 110 centimeters.
cues.zh: 例如這個區間是 60 到 70 公分，依此類推，一直到 100 到 110 公分。

cues.en: So then we have to just ask these penguins if they are in this height group or this height group or this height group.
cues.zh: 接著只要問企鵝，屬於這個身高組、這個組，還是這個組。

cues.en: And that's the sort of thing that penguins, if they could understand our language, could be able to respond to.
cues.zh: 如果企鵝能理解我們的語言，應該就能回答這種問題。

cues.en: And we could produce a plot like this.
cues.zh: 就能產生這樣的圖。

cues.en: So the conclusions here are that numerical data must be converted to discrete type in order to make a bar plot visualization like this.
cues.zh: 結論是，要做出這種長條圖視覺化，數值資料必須轉成離散類型。

cues.en: Now, you might ask, why did I choose five bins and why did I pick these boundaries?
cues.zh: 你可能問，為什麼選五個區間，又為什麼選這些邊界？

cues.en: Why not 60 to 65 and 65 to 70 and so on?
cues.zh: 為什麼不是 60 到 65、65 到 70，依此類推？

cues.en: Well, I could have also done that.
cues.zh: 也可以那樣做。

cues.en: It turns out that been no and been boundaries are how you define these boundaries here.
cues.zh: 區間數與區間邊界，也就是如何定義這些邊界，

cues.en: These are important and non-trivial parameters of making these kinds of visualizations.
cues.zh: 是建立這類視覺化時，重要而且不簡單的參數。

cues.en: And exactly how you do that or make those decisions is beyond the scope of this video, because that's related to histogram.
cues.zh: 確切該怎麼決定，超出這部影片範圍，因為與直方圖有關。

cues.en: So you will learn more about this concept in later videos.
cues.zh: 稍後影片會再學到這個概念。

cues.en: Now, I am kind of suggesting that this is a bar plot if you want to get really super duper technical.
cues.zh: 我一直暗示這是長條圖，但如果真的要非常嚴格地講，

cues.en: It turns out this is actually not a bar plot.
cues.zh: 這其實不是長條圖。

cues.en: This is called a histogram.
cues.zh: 它叫做直方圖。

cues.en: So this is a histogram.
cues.zh: 這是直方圖。

cues.en: Not a bar plot, because I'm representing numeric discrete data in ordered bins like this.
cues.zh: 而非長條圖，因為我是用這些有順序的區間，表示離散數值資料。

cues.en: So technically, this is a histogram, but it doesn't really matter.
cues.zh: 所以嚴格來說是直方圖，但其實沒那麼重要。

cues.en: People use those terms interchangeably.
cues.zh: 人們會混用這些詞。

cues.en: So, you know, I'm not going to give someone a hard time if they call this a bar plot.
cues.zh: 如果有人把它稱為長條圖，我不會為難他。

cues.en: Instead of calling it a histogram.
cues.zh: 即使應該叫直方圖。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So I'm going to talk more about histograms later in the course, both in this section and in later sections as well.
cues.zh: 課程稍後會再談直方圖，包括這一節與後續章節。

cues.en: But I want to get back to these bar plots.
cues.zh: 但現在想回到長條圖。

cues.en: Let's go back to this example where we asked people, how do you get your news?
cues.zh: 回到這個例子，問人們如何取得新聞。

cues.en: Now, let's say we surveyed two groups of people.
cues.zh: 假設調查兩群人。

cues.en: We have the millennials here on 20 to 40 years old and the boomers here around 50 to 70 years old.
cues.zh: 這裡是 20 到 40 歲左右的千禧世代，這裡是 50 到 70 歲左右的嬰兒潮世代。

cues.en: So you can imagine that younger people versus older people get their news from slightly different sources, different distributions of of media that they are getting their news from.
cues.zh: 可以想像，年輕人與年長者取得新聞的來源稍有不同，使用的媒體分布不同。

cues.en: So we could make a plot that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 可以畫成這樣。

cues.en: So here we have two bars, a pair of bars for each x axis tech or each medium presented on the x axis.
cues.zh: 每個 x 軸刻度、也就是每種媒體，都有一對長條。

cues.en: So it's kind of interesting, not so surprising.
cues.zh: 有點意思，但不太意外。

cues.en: The boomers are getting their information more from TV compared to the millennials and the millennials are surfing the Web for their news compared to the boomers.
cues.zh: 相較千禧世代，嬰兒潮世代更多從電視取得資訊；相較嬰兒潮世代，千禧世代更多上網看新聞。

cues.en: Now, this is just one way to visualize the data.
cues.zh: 這只是視覺化資料的一種方法。

cues.en: We can take exactly this same data and group the bars in a different way so I can group the bar as this way.
cues.zh: 也能用完全相同的資料，改變長條分組方式，像這樣分組。

cues.en: So now all the younger participants are over here and all the older respondents are over here.
cues.zh: 現在所有年輕參與者在這邊，所有年長受訪者在那邊。

cues.en: This means we actually repeat these media here.
cues.zh: 代表這些媒體標籤會重複。

cues.en: So TV, TV, newspaper, newspaper and so on.
cues.zh: 例如電視、電視，報紙、報紙，依此類推。

cues.en: So which of these two bar plots is correct?
cues.zh: 這兩種長條圖，哪個正確？

cues.en: Well, obviously they're both correct.
cues.zh: 顯然都正確。

cues.en: It's a trick question.
cues.zh: 這是陷阱題。

cues.en: But the question is the real question is, which is not a trick question is what kinds of information does this organization versus this organization convey?
cues.zh: 真正的問題，不是陷阱題，是這種排列方式與另一種排列方式，各自傳達什麼資訊？

cues.en: And that turns out to be really not trivial at all.
cues.zh: 這其實一點也不簡單。

cues.en: So the way that you group data in bar plots is going to have an impact on how people interpret your results.
cues.zh: 長條圖中資料分組的方式，會影響人們如何解讀結果。

cues.en: Even though the data are all exactly the same in these two plots.
cues.zh: 即使兩張圖的資料完全相同。

cues.en: So here what you're I what your eye is drawn towards is the comparisons within each media type and then the differences between the group.
cues.zh: 這裡，目光會被引導去比較每種媒體，以及群體之間的差異。

cues.en: So what your eye sees is while the boomers are going for TV and not the millennials and the millennials are going for Internet and not the boomers.
cues.zh: 看到的是，嬰兒潮世代偏好電視，千禧世代不然；千禧世代偏好網路，嬰兒潮世代不然。

cues.en: In contrast, when we look at this organization of exactly the same data, your eye gives you a different impression.
cues.zh: 相反地，看相同資料的這種排列方式，視覺會產生不同印象。

cues.en: So what you're thinking about now is within the group of younger respondents.
cues.zh: 現在想的是，在年輕受訪者群體中，

cues.en: Most people go for Internet to get news.
cues.zh: 大多數人從網路取得新聞。

cues.en: And some people word of mouth.
cues.zh: 有些人靠口耳相傳。

cues.en: And, you know, not so many for these two sources.
cues.zh: 使用這兩個來源的人，則沒那麼多。

cues.en: And then for the older respondents, we get more information from TV and less from these other sources and so on.
cues.zh: 年長受訪者更多從電視取得資訊，較少從其他來源，依此類推。

cues.en: They can see it's you know, it's a little bit of a different interpretation for these two organizations.
cues.zh: 可見這兩種排列，帶來稍微不同的解讀。

cues.en: So there's no right or wrong, but it is something that you should think about when creating multi-dimensional data on a single graph like this.
cues.zh: 所以沒有對錯，但在單一圖表呈現這種多維資料時，應該考慮這件事。

cues.en: Now, I want to extend the concept of bar plots a little bit to tell you about error bars.
cues.zh: 現在延伸長條圖概念，介紹誤差線。

cues.en: So these are called errorbars.
cues.zh: 這些叫做誤差線。

cues.en: So it looks like.
cues.zh: 看起來像，

cues.en: So it is a bar plot.
cues.zh: 就是一張長條圖，

cues.en: And then on top of it, we have these like these lines.
cues.zh: 上方再加上這些線。

cues.en: It's a vertical line.
cues.zh: 一條垂直線。

cues.en: And then a little horizontal hashmark here just to kind of help you appreciate where the top and the bottom are.
cues.zh: 以及這裡的一小段水平刻痕，幫助看清上端與下端。

cues.en: So the question is, what do these errorbars show?
cues.zh: 問題是，誤差線顯示什麼？

cues.en: This one is also kind of funny because it it goes negative.
cues.zh: 這個也有點好笑，因為延伸到負值。

cues.en: It goes in getting like negative percent people to respond.
cues.zh: 變成有負百分比的人，回答，

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 是，

cues.en: To word of mouth.
cues.zh: 對口耳相傳這個選項。

cues.en: So what do these errorbars show?
cues.zh: 這些誤差線顯示什麼？

cues.en: Well, we actually don't know.
cues.zh: 其實不知道。

cues.en: It doesn't have any enough information on this plot to tell us what these errorbars show.
cues.zh: 圖上沒有足夠資訊，告訴我們誤差線顯示什麼。

cues.en: There are a couple of features that errorbars often show.
cues.zh: 誤差線經常顯示幾種特性。

cues.en: They are typically one of these three standard deviation or the standard error or confidence intervals around some parameter estimate.
cues.zh: 通常是這三者之一：標準差、標準誤，或某個參數估計值周圍的信賴區間。

cues.en: And how do we know which one is being plotted?
cues.zh: 怎麼知道畫的是哪一個？

cues.en: Well, in this case, we actually don't.
cues.zh: 這個例子，確實不知道。

cues.en: If, by the way, if you're not really familiar with these terms or maybe you've heard of these terms, but you don't really know what they mean.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，如果不熟悉這些術語，或聽過但不知道確切意思，

cues.en: Don't worry about it for now.
cues.zh: 目前不用擔心。

cues.en: You will learn all about these different measures later on in the course.
cues.zh: 稍後課程會學到這些不同的量。

cues.en: The point for now in this video is that errorbars are sometimes ambiguous because unfortunately, fairly
cues.zh: 這部影片目前的重點，是誤差線有時有歧義，因為很不幸，相當，

cues.en: often, not all the time, but often enough people create errorbars without indicating what the error bars actually show.
cues.zh: 常見，雖然不是每次，但夠常發生：人們畫了誤差線，卻沒標示它真正代表什麼。

cues.en: So error bars are sometimes just adding more confusion to the plot than information.
cues.zh: 所以誤差線有時只是增加困惑，而非資訊。

cues.en: OK.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that might lead you to wonder, can errorbars be misinterpreted or used for evil purposes?
cues.zh: 你可能因此想，誤差線會被誤解，或用來做壞事嗎？

cues.en: Well, so the answer is yes to at least the first question.
cues.zh: 至少第一個問題，答案是會。

cues.en: Not sure about evil purposes, but it is important to use error bars correctly and explain them clearly when you are using errorbars in a plot.
cues.zh: 不確定做壞事，但正確使用誤差線，並在圖中清楚解釋，很重要。

cues.en: Again, I'm going to talk more about these things later on in the course.
cues.zh: 課程稍後會再談。

cues.en: The main point for now is to appreciate that just because you see some errorbars in a plot doesn't mean that.
cues.zh: 目前重點，是理解看到圖裡有誤差線，不代表，

cues.en: They mean they indicate what you think they might indicate.
cues.zh: 它就代表你以為的意思。

cues.en: They could mean something very different from what you might naively or intuitively expect them to mean.
cues.zh: 它可能和你直覺、天真預期的意思，完全不同。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that was a fun video I showed you about bar plots and how to interpret bar plots.
cues.zh: 這是有趣的影片，介紹了長條圖，以及如何解讀。

cues.en: We discussed the types of data that can be used in bar plots.
cues.zh: 談了哪些資料類型適用於長條圖。

cues.en: I also introduced you to the concept of histograms, which you will learn more about later.
cues.zh: 也介紹了直方圖的概念，之後會深入學習。

cues.en: And I showed you how different ways of organizing and labelling bar plots can actually change the way
cues.zh: 還展示不同組織與標示長條圖的方式，如何改變，

cues.en: that people are gathering information about the data based on your bar plots and I introduce you to error bars.
cues.zh: 人們根據圖表取得資料資訊的方式，並介紹誤差線。

cues.en: In the main important point there was that when plots have error bars in them, but those error bars are not clearly indicated.
cues.zh: 最重要的重點，是圖中有誤差線，卻沒有清楚標示時，

cues.en: Then you don't necessarily know what those error bars are actually showing.
cues.zh: 就不一定知道誤差線真正顯示什麼。

cues.en: You have to be mindful of that.
cues.zh: 必須留意這一點。
